name: CUS202-project
description: A course-material access bundle for AI agents: one read-only Canvas MCP server plus a small set of usage-discipline skills, with an optional tier that must be enabled explicitly.

study.context: CUS202 mini-project, Group 2, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
study.note: The four default skills are the variables. The Canvas server sits outside the measurement and is set up in every session, because it only supplies material.
study.participants: About 12 to 15 students drawn from the 19 enrolled in the class.
study.focus: Hallucination reduction and text quality. The Canvas server is infrastructure.

components.description: Read-only access to canvas.polyu.edu.hk via the Canvas REST API. All requests are GET, restricted to /api/v1/, with a page cap.
components.auth: browser login session cookie stored at ~/.canvas-polyu/session.json, or a personal access token if the institution issues one
components.off_by_default_because: A server needs Node.js and a browser login. The four default skills work without it, so it is opt in.

components.description: Entry skill. Decides whether a question needs course material, calls the right server tool, and hands the draft to cite-check.
Answer questions about course requirements only from retrieved course pages, and record the page each claim came from.
Before delivery, verify that every quoted requirement exists in the retrieved material. Blocks citations that cannot be traced.
Answer-first, short-form output shaped for a reader who needs the next action immediately.
components.activation: manual only — the skill sets disable-model-invocation: true, so it cannot fire on its own. A participant has to invoke it.
components.in_core_because: Raised in our depth interviews: students described weak prompts producing long, unfocused answers, and reported that forcing short answer-first output made their follow-up questions sharper. Being manually invoked, it is inert unless a participant turns it on, so it does not contaminate a session that leaves it alone.
components.study_note: Record whether it was invoked per session (log field adhd_mode). Sessions that invoke it are analysed separately, and style metrics are excluded from the outcome set either way.

components.description: Removes signs of AI-generated writing from text.
components.off_by_default_because: It rewrites output, so it changes any style-based quality score.
components.why_in_default: It is the text-quality half of the set. It rewrites surface, so it stays out of style-based scoring in the study, but it belongs to the same job as the other three.

components.description: Lets the agent watch a video: downloads it, extracts frames and transcribes the audio.
components.enable_when: You need the agent to read a lecture recording.
components.off_by_default_because: High token and network cost, and it only serves one task type.

components.description: A multi-skill pipeline for research, writing, review and revision.
components.enable_when: You are writing a paper rather than answering a coursework question.
components.off_by_default_because: Very broad trigger surface. In testing it takes over the turn and displaces the course-material skills.
components.attribution: Based on Academic Research Skills by Cheng-I Wu, https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills

components.description: 38 small skills localised into Chinese: 20 engineering, 7 productivity, 7 in progress, 4 misc. The productivity group is domain-neutral. grilling interviews the user about a plan in rounds, with a recommended answer per question, until no branch is unsettled. to-questionnaire turns a decision the user cannot answer alone into a form for someone else.
components.enable_when: You are scoping anything with more than one decision in it, or doing TypeScript work.
components.off_by_default_because: 38 skills make a very broad trigger surface. Call it by name, /zh-grilling, rather than leaving it to auto-selection.
components.rationale: Interview data: students reported the project drifting when nobody forced the open questions onto the table. A skill that asks back does the job a supervisor does.
